newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot gas prices mixed, export values gain.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot gas prices mixed, export values gain.

text.p: Canadian spot natgas prices were mixed Monday in thin trade, with the domestic market steady to down slightly, while export values gained on stronger U.S. numbers, market sources said.

"Canada (domestic prices) softened up a bit today. Nova receipts are actually showing up and the B.C. plant is back on line," said one Calgary-based trader, referring to the return over the weekend of Westcoast Energy's Fort Nelson gas processing plant in British Columbia.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was quoted in a range between C$1.55 and C$1.60, off slightly from Friday.
July gas at AECO was quoted in the high-C$1.50s, down from the low-C$1.60s on Friday.

Westcoast said Monday that the Fort Nelson gas plant had returned to full operation yesterday. The plant, which had been shut for scheduled maintenance since June 10, restarted Thursday but was shut again Friday and a force majeure was declared because of problems with the quality of gas being delivered to the plant.
Export prices rebounded with a firmer U.S. market, which was boosted by the season's first heat wave in the Midwest and Northeast.
Gas at Sumas, Washington, was pegged in the mid-$1.20s per mmBtu, up almost five cents from Friday.
And prices at Niagara in eastern Canada gained four cents to about the $2.44 per mmBtu level.
NYMEX's July Henry Hub natgas futures closed 1.1 cents higher today at $2.246.
